question: Which quantum states of phonons have been successfully prepared?

ingredients.name: answer_critical_0
ingredients.criterion: Answer enumerates the phonon quantum states successfully prepared: the quantum ground state, single-phonon and multi-phonon Fock states, superpositions of Fock states, and coherent states.
examples: ground states, Fock states, their superpositions, and coherent states have all been prepared
experiments have realized the phonon ground state, number states with n up to several phonons, and coherent states

ingredients.name: answer_critical_1
ingredients.criterion: Answer identifies the phonon ground state as successfully prepared, reached by cooling a ~6 GHz microwave-frequency mechanical mode ('quantum drum') below ~0.1 K in a dilution refrigerator.
examples: a 6 GHz mechanical mode was cooled to its ground state via conventional cryogenic cooling below 0.1 K in a dilution refrigerator
ground state achieved when thermal occupation drops below one phonon

ingredients.name: answer_critical_2
ingredients.criterion: Answer states that a single phonon (individual quantum excitation) was controllably created in the resonator via time-domain control of the qubit–resonator interaction, with its exchange between resonator and qubit observed.
examples: controllably create an individual quantum excitation (a phonon) in the resonator
single-phonon Fock state prepared and shown to swap between resonator and qubit

ingredients.name: answer_critical_3
ingredients.criterion: Answer states that multi-phonon Fock states and their superpositions were prepared and fully tomographically reconstructed in a high-overtone bulk acoustic-wave resonator (HBAR) coupled to a transmon qubit.
examples: Fock states of phonons and their superpositions prepared inside an HBAR with full quantum tomography
N-phonon number states created and tomographically reconstructed in a bulk acoustic-wave resonator

ingredients.name: answer_critical_4
ingredients.criterion: Answer mentions that a coherent state of the mechanical resonator was generated by a classical excitation, with the measured qubit response agreeing with theory.
examples: a classical drive generated a coherent state of the mechanical resonator
coherent-state qubit response in good agreement with theory

ingredients.name: valuable_0
ingredients.criterion: Answer explains that state preparation and verification were enabled by coupling a superconducting qubit to the mechanical/acoustic resonator (circuit quantum acoustodynamics), e.g., a transmon flip-chip coupled to the HBAR in the strong-coupling regime, providing quantum-limited measurement.
examples: a superconducting qubit coupled to the resonator enables state preparation and quantum-limited measurement
transmon qubit flip-chip coupled to the HBAR enables phonon state control

ingredients.name: valuable_1
ingredients.criterion: Answer includes quantified verification of the ground state, e.g., maximum phonon number <0.07, corresponding to >93% ground-state probability.
examples: qubit-based measurement bounds the thermal phonon occupancy below one

ingredients.name: valuable_2
ingredients.criterion: Answer notes related demonstrations on other acoustic platforms (e.g., surface acoustic wave resonators coupled to superconducting qubits) and/or the significance of the results, such as showing quantum mechanics applies to a macroscopic object and that deeper strong coupling enables more complex states.
examples: similar quantum-state demonstration reported using surface acoustic waves
evidence that quantum mechanics applies to an object visible to the naked eye
